E-131: Detection delay under adaptive (sched + cache): cpu 284 ms, random-io 286, sequential-io 1,516, network 289, interactive 407. Under round_robin + lru: 303, 289, 287, 304, 299 ms.

RQ4: four of five phases are recognised within 284-407 ms. The sequential-I/O phase took 1,516 ms under adaptive because read-ahead makes the reads hit the cache from the first sample (25,000-31,000 reads per 250 ms): the readers barely block and look INTERACTIVE for about 1.2 s before IO_BOUND. Throughput is at full speed from the first sample, so this is a labelling delay, not a performance loss. Phases were 8 s, not the 60 s of NEW_EXPLANATION §36.

M17: after F-122 the adaptive policy keeps the median interactive latency at 14 µs (round-robin: 19.5 ms), but its p99 (3.0 ms) is 12x the low-latency policy's, and it trades the CPU-bound build work away: 92 % fewer build jobs than round-robin and 79 % fewer than low-latency, while the TCP stream runs 2.6x faster than under low-latency. Cause, visible in the thread classes: busy streaming threads are classified IO_BOUND (many I/O calls, short bursts) and get priority 8 over the MIXED build workers (12); the IO_BOUND rule does not consider CPU share. On this mix the adaptive scheduler does NOT beat the hand-picked low-latency policy. Media: NOT RUN (no audio/video path); build = CPU proxy (no compiler).
Add CPU share to the IO_BOUND rule (a busy streamer is not I/O-bound) and rerun E-129 and this suite.
